questions.question: Study of motion of an object with the causes of its motion is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Dynamics. Dynamics is the branch of physics that studies motion of objects along with the forces that cause the motion.

questions.question: Laws of motion are presented by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Isaac Newton. The three laws of motion were formulated by Sir Isaac Newton.

questions.question: Laws of motion are described in the famous book of Isaac Newton:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Principia Mathematica. Newton published his laws in the book "Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica" in 1687.

questions.question: ______ can change the state of rest or motion and direction of motion of a body.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Force. Force can change speed, direction, or state (rest/motion) of an object.

questions.question: Who observed that it is easy to move or stop light objects than heavier ones?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Galileo. Galileo observed that heavier objects resist motion more than lighter ones.

questions.question: Newton’s first law of motion is also known as law of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Inertia. First law explains inertia — resistance to change in motion.

questions.question: ______ of a body is its property due to which it resists any change in its state of rest or motion.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Inertia. Inertia is the resistance to change in motion.

questions.question: Inertia of a body depends on:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Mass. Greater mass means greater inertia.

questions.question: ______ is the quantity of motion of body possesses due to its mass and velocity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Momentum. Momentum = mass × velocity.

questions.question: Momentum is ______ quantity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Vector. Momentum has magnitude and direction → vector.

questions.question: Laws of motion describe the relationship between force and ______ of a body.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Motion. Newton’s laws relate force to motion (especially acceleration).

questions.question: The impact of bullet is so strong when it is fired from the gun due to its:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Greater momentum. A bullet fired from a gun possesses high velocity and therefore a large momentum, resulting in high impact force.

questions.question: Which property of a body cannot change if a force is applied to it?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Mass. An applied force can change an object's velocity, shape, and size, but the mass of the object remains invariant in classical mechanics.

questions.question: When a bus takes a sharp turn, passengers fall outward due to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Inertia. Body wants to continue straight due to inertia.

questions.question: Newton’s first law is applicable in the:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Absence of net force. Newton's first law describes motion when the net external force acting on a body is zero (absence of net force).

questions.question: A body produces ______ when a force acts on it.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Acceleration. Force causes acceleration (F = ma).

questions.question: Acceleration produced in a moving body is always in direction of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Force. Acceleration direction is same as net force direction.

questions.question: Newton’s second law is applicable in the:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Presence of net force. Second law applies when net force ≠ 0.

questions.question: One Newton is the force that produces acceleration of ______ in a body of mass 1 kg.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 1 m/s². 1 N = force needed to produce 1 m/s² in 1 kg mass.

questions.question: If force = 70 N and mass = 10 kg, acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 7 m/s². a = F/m = 70/10 = 7 m/s²

questions.question: If force is halved and mass constant, acceleration will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): One half. a ∝ F → half force → half acceleration.

questions.question: The quantity of motion possessed by a body is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Momentum. Quantity of motion = momentum.

questions.question: The force of gravity acting on a body is known as:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Weight. Weight = gravitational force on body.

questions.question: SI unit of mass is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Kilogram. Mass SI unit = kilogram.

questions.question: SI unit of weight is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Newton. Weight is force → unit Newton.

questions.question: Mass of body is measured by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Beam balance. Beam balance compares mass.

questions.question: Weight is measured by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Spring balance. Weight is measured using spring or digital balance.

questions.question: ______ of a body remains same everywhere.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Mass. Mass is an intrinsic quantity of matter and remains constant everywhere, whereas weight varies with local gravitational field strength.

questions.question: Weight of a body depends on:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Gravitational acceleration. Weight = m × g It depends on gravitational acceleration (g).

questions.question: Mass is a ______ quantity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Scalar. Mass has only magnitude, no direction → scalar quantity.

questions.question: Weight is a ______ quantity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Vector. Weight is a force. Force has direction → vector quantity.

questions.question: To every action there is always an equal but opposite ______.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Reaction. Newton’s third law: Every action has equal and opposite reaction.

questions.question: If a block is hanged with the help of a string, the weight of block is balanced by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Tension. In equilibrium, upward tension equals downward weight.

questions.question: Spider web remains intact with roof owing to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Tension. Tension force in the web keeps it attached.

questions.question: There are ______ cases of motion of a body hanging with the help of string.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 2. In FBISE Class 9 physics, two standard cases of motion of bodies connected by a string passing over a pulley are studied: Case 1 (both bodies move vertically) and Case 2 (one body moves vertically and the other horizontally).

questions.question: ______ is used to find acceleration due to gravity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Atwood machine. Atwood machine helps calculate acceleration and gravitational acceleration.

questions.question: The momentum of an isolated system remains:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Constant. Law of conservation of momentum → total momentum remains constant.

questions.question: Jet engines work on the principle of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Law of conservation of momentum. Backward momentum of gases → forward thrust (Newton’s 3rd law).

questions.question: Rate of change of momentum is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Force. According to Newton's second law in terms of momentum, the rate of change of momentum equals the applied force (F = Δp / Δt).

questions.question: The force that retards motion of one body on another is known as:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Friction. Friction opposes motion.

questions.question: Maximum value of friction is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Limiting. Limiting friction is maximum static friction before motion starts.

questions.question: Kinetic friction is always less than ______ friction.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Static. Static friction > kinetic friction.

questions.question: Ratio of limiting friction to normal reaction is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Coefficient of friction. μ = Limiting friction / Normal reaction.

questions.question: SI unit of coefficient of friction is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): No unit. It is a ratio → unitless quantity.

questions.question: Rolling friction is almost ______ times less than sliding friction.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): 50. Rolling friction is approximately 50 times smaller than sliding friction.

questions.question: Coefficient of friction depends upon:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Nature of surfaces. It depends on the nature/material of surfaces in contact.

questions.question: Fast-moving objects are shaped streamline to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Reduce air friction. Streamlining reduces air resistance.

questions.question: Motion of moon around earth is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Circular. Moon revolves in nearly circular orbit.

questions.question: Banking of road means outer edge is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Raised. Outer edge is raised to provide centripetal force.

questions.question: Water from wet clothes is forced out due to lack of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Centripetal force. Water cannot get centripetal force → moves outward.

questions.question: Separation of cream from milk is based on:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Centrifugal force. Centrifugal force pushes heavier particles outward.

questions.question: Friction of liquid is ______ than solid.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Less. Liquid friction (viscosity) is less than solid friction.

questions.question: When horse pulls cart, reaction is on the:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Horse. According to Newton’s Third Law, for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. When the horse pushes against the ground (action), the ground pushes the horse forward (reaction). Similarly, if the horse pulls the cart forward, the cart pulls back on the horse.

questions.question: ______ of body does not remain same everywhere.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Weight. Weight depends on gravitational acceleration.

questions.question: A body has weight 30 N. Force required to move it upward with acceleration 4 m/s² is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 42 N. Weight = mg = 30 N m = 30/10 = 3 kg (approx g=10) F = m(g + a) = 3(10 + 4) = 42 N

questions.question: If speed is doubled, centripetal force becomes:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 4 Fc. F ∝ v² If v doubles → force becomes 4 times.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Gravitational force. Gravitational force acts without physical contact.

questions.question: Describe a situation where you experience both contact and non-contact forces simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Electrostatic force. In daily life, we experience contact forces (friction, tension) and non-contact forces (gravity, magnetism) together.

questions.question: Which force opposes the relative motion of two surfaces in contact?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Friction. Friction resists motion between surfaces.

questions.question: An object hanging from a spring experiences an upward force known as:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Tension. The string or spring provides tension force upward.

questions.question: Which of the following is the weakest fundamental force?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Gravitational force. Gravitational force is by far the weakest of the four fundamental forces of nature (approximately 10³⁸ times weaker than the strong nuclear force).

questions.question: Which force holds quarks together inside protons and neutrons?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Strong force. Strong nuclear force binds quarks.

questions.question: Which force attracts electrons and protons in an atom?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Electromagnetic force. Opposite electric charges attract due to electromagnetic force.

questions.question: Which force is responsible for certain radioactive decay?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Weak force. Weak nuclear force causes beta decay.

questions.question: Which is the strongest fundamental force?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Strong force. Strong nuclear force is strongest.

questions.question: Which force holds atoms together in a molecule?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Electromagnetic force. Chemical bonds are due to electromagnetic force.

questions.question: In free-body diagram of book on table, upward force is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Normal force. Table pushes book upward with normal force.

questions.question: In free fall near Earth, which force acts?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Weight (gravitational force). In ideal free fall near the Earth, air resistance is neglected and only the gravitational force (weight) acts on the body.

questions.question: If 8 N right and 6 N left act on object, resultant is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 2 N right. 8 − 6 = 2 N toward right.

questions.question: If car moves with constant velocity, then:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Net force is zero. Constant velocity → acceleration = 0 → net force = 0.

questions.question: Inertia depends on:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Mass. Inertia ∝ mass.

questions.question: Force can change velocity by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Both direction and speed. Velocity is a vector quantity having both speed and direction; an applied force can change speed, direction, or both.

questions.question: Action and reaction do not cancel because:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Act on different objects. They act on two different bodies.

questions.question: Relativistic mechanics applies at:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Near speed of light. At very high speeds near light speed.

questions.question: Which is NOT affected by gravitational field?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Pressure. Mass is the actual amount of “stuff” or matter inside an object. It stays the same no matter where you are in the universe because it doesn’t depend on gravity. Weight: Changes directly with the gravitational field (W = mg). Pressure: In fluids, pressure depends on gravity (P = ρ gh). Volume: While volume is usually constant, in large-scale physics (like stars or planets), gravity can compress objects and change their volume. Key Difference If you take a 10kg bowling ball to the Moon, its mass is still 10kg, but its weight will feel much lighter because the Moon’s gravitational field is weaker.

questions.question: Weight of 10 kg object (g = 9.8 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 98.1 N. W = mg = 10 × 9.81 = 98.1 N

questions.question: Which remains constant everywhere?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Mass. Mass is constant.

questions.question: If weight = 98 N and mass = 10 kg, g is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 9.8 m/s². g = 98/10 = 9.8 m/s²

questions.question: Which has greatest momentum?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 1000 kg × 1 m/s. All equal to 1000 kg·m/s.

questions.question: If an object is stationary, what is its momentum?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Zero. Momentum = m × v If velocity = 0 → momentum = 0.

questions.question: Which factor affects impulse?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): All of the above. Impulse is defined as J = F × Δt = Δp = m(v_f - v_i). It depends on applied force, time, mass, and velocity change.

questions.question: If time of impact increases, the force required to change momentum:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Decreases. Since Force = Δp / Δt, increasing the collision duration Δt reduces the average impact force experienced for a given momentum change.

questions.question: What does mass measure?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Quantity of matter. Mass measures amount of matter.

questions.question: Define weight:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Force due to gravity. Weight is defined as the force of gravity acting on an object (W = mg).

questions.question: Purpose of a force meter is to measure:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Force. Force meter measures force in Newton.

questions.question: Weight of object on Earth = 25 N. g = 9.8 N/kg. What is mass?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 2.6 kg. m = W/g = 25 / 9.8 ≈ 2.55 kg ≈ 2.6 kg.

questions.question: When a force is applied, which effect cannot occur?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Object remains still. In classical physics, mass is a constant property of an object. Applying a force can change how an object moves or how it is shaped, but it cannot make the actual matter inside the object disappear. (b) Object remains still: This happens if the force is balanced by friction or another opposing force. (c) & (d) Slows down / Speeds up: These are standard effects of force (acceleration/deceleration) as described by Newton’s Second Law. Key takeaway: Force affects motion and shape, but it does not affect mass.

questions.question: An object is in complete equilibrium when:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): No translational or rotational effects. Complete equilibrium requires satisfying both conditions: first condition (ΣF = 0, no translational acceleration) and second condition (Στ = 0, no angular acceleration).

questions.question: Example of non-contact force:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Gravity. Gravity acts without contact.

questions.question: Force responsible for stretching elastic band:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Tension. Stretching creates tension force.

questions.question: Free body diagrams show:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Forces acting on object. They show all forces on an object.

questions.question: According to Newton’s first law, object remains at rest unless acted upon by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Unbalanced force. An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external (unbalanced) force.

questions.question: Newton’s laws do not accurately describe motion:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): At very high speeds. Relativity needed at high speeds.

questions.question: Force holding nucleus together:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Strong force. Strong nuclear force binds nucleons.

questions.question: Nobel Prize discovery related to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Unification of weak & electromagnetic. Electroweak theory unified weak and electromagnetic forces.

questions.question: Force governing charged particles:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Electromagnetic force. Charged particles interact via electromagnetic force.

questions.question: If impulse is zero, momentum:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Remains constant. Impulse equals change in momentum (J = Δp). If impulse is zero, Δp = 0, which means momentum remains constant.

questions.question: Car mass 1000 kg, velocity 20 m/s. Momentum?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 20000. p = 1000 × 20 = 20000 kg·m/s.

questions.question: If time of collision doubles, impulse:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Same. Impulse depends on change in momentum, not time directly. If momentum change same → impulse same.

questions.question: Which violates conservation of momentum?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Car braking on a road. When a moving car suddenly brakes: Friction between tires and road acts as external force.Car’s momentum decreases.Momentum is transferred to the Earth.So for the car alone, momentum is not conserved.

questions.question: In closed system, if one object gains momentum, another:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Gains equal and opposite momentum. Total momentum constant → equal and opposite change.

questions.question: Dynamics is the branch of physics which deals with:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Motion and its causes'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The SI unit of force is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Newton'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: One Newton is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): '1 kg·m/s²'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Friction'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The force which opposes motion is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Friction'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The property of a body to resist any change in its state is called:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Inertia'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Inertia'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

options.A: A net external force acts on it

questions.question: Newton’s second law gives the definition of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Force'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If mass = 2 kg and acceleration = 3 m/s², then force = ?

questions.question: A man applies a force but the object doesn’t move. The work done is:

questions.question: A spring balances measures:

questions.question: Which force is responsible for wearing of shoe soles?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Friction'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: 1 kg-weight is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): '9.8 N'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Newton’s third law states:

options.A: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Every action has an equal and opposite reaction'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Recoil of gun is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Newton’s 3rd law'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The action and reaction forces act on:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Different bodies'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is:

questions.question: Mass of a body is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Constant everywhere'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Weight is defined as:

questions.question: Weight of an object on the moon is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'One-sixth of Earth'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The SI unit of weight is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Newton'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: If mass is 50 kg, then weight on Earth is:

questions.question: When a body is at rest, the net force acting on it is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Zero'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The force responsible for holding planets in orbit is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Gravitational force'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The mass of a body is measured by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Beam balance'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Friction always acts in:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Opposite direction of motion'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Which of the following is a field force?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Gravitational force'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The inertia of rest means:

options.A: Body remains at rest until forced
options.D: Body changes motion on its own

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 'Body remains at rest until forced'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: When force is doubled and mass remains constant, acceleration:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Doubles'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The relationship between mass, force, and acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'f = ma'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Unit of frictional force is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 'Newton'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The gravitational field of Earth is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): '9.8 N/kg'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The third law pair forces always:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Act on different bodies'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: Gravitational force is always:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): 'Attractive'. In FBISE Grade 9 Physics Unit 3 (Dynamics), this is a standard curriculum property and board-examined definition.

questions.question: The tendency of a body to stay at rest or continue motion is due to:
